## Summary

**Failure reproduced:** `python reproduce.py` returned exit `1` (`pre_fix_expected_failure`). The workflow swallows the real exception, but digging it out revealed `ValueError: axis 1 index 8 exceeds matrix dimension 3` in `SciPyCanonBackend._reshape_parametric`.

**Root cause:** The tracking workflow stores dynamics data as 3-D `cp.Parameter((steps, state_dim, state_dim))` and indexes it per timestep (`params["A"][t-1] @ ...`). N-D expressions force CVXPY off the default CPP backend onto the SCIPY backend. There, `_reshape_parametric` receives the constant data as a column vector `v` stacking `param_size` slices (one per parameter element), each of length `m*k`. The buggy code used the *parameter-element index* as the within-matrix position (`param_idx % m`, `param_idx // m`) and deduplicated by it. That only happens to hold for non-indexed 2-D parameters (where element index == within-slice position); for an indexed N-D parameter the two differ, so the computed column indices ran out of bounds.

**Fix** (`source/cvxpy/lin_ops/backends/scipy_backend.py:355`): `_reshape_parametric` now mirrors `_reshape_nonparametric` with the slice count equal to `param_size` — decompose each nonzero into its slice (parameter element) and within-slice position, map the position to matrix `(row, col)` in column-major order, and stack slices vertically into `(param_size*m, k)`. The incorrect `np.unique` deduplication is removed so all contributions are retained (SciPy sums any true duplicates). This preserves the existing 2-D parametric path exactly.

**Validation:**
- Public smoke test → exit `0`, `workflow_completed`, optimal, objective `0.262679`.
- 21 workflow-pattern cases (7 seed/dim/timestep configs × SCS/CLARABEL/OSQP) match an independent baked-constant ground truth (CPP backend, no Parameters) with optimal status and dynamics residuals at solver tolerance (~1e-8 for SCS, ~1e-16 for CLARABEL/OSQP).
- Edge cases pass: `var @ indexed-3D-param` (rmul), `indexed-4D-param @ var`, and multi-slice sums.
- No regression: 2-D parametric mul/rmul/mul_elem and DPP re-solve all unchanged.

The fix is general (no fixture hard-coding, no reformulation, no canned trajectories). Pre-existing, out-of-scope gaps (direct batched N-D matmul and elementwise multiply of indexed N-D params — both also broken on the COO backend and not used by the workflow) are unchanged.
